[32560 Information Systems Architecture Design | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This postgraduate subject explores the role of architecture in agile methodologies, particularly relevant for those considering the value of architecture when best practices encourage rapid iteration over detailed planning. In learning about Enterprise Architecture, you will focus on on strategic IT alignment with business needs in a world where exhaustive detail is impractical due to constant organisational evolution. You'll model crucial organisational aspects and develop a toolkit for articulating this information.
You'll examine the tactical delivery of IT soultions and learn to integrate architectural considerations with agile teams, determining when to establish system aspects upfront versus through the agile cycle. The subject enhances your ability to apply architectural patterns, avoid common pitfalls, and effectively model architectures with clear, understandable diagrams.

[32560 Information Systems Architecture Design | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject will be taught using a flipped-learning approach. Pre-recorded lectures, readings and other self-paced online activities will allow students to learn and test their understanding of subject content in their own time. Face-to-face learning will be focused on applying, reinforcing, and reflecting upon this knowledge.

 The expected time commitment includes:

 - approximately 1.5 hours per week of self-paced online activities (primarily pre-recorded lectures)
 - up to 3 hours per week of face-to-face tutorials (the majority are expected to take 1.5 hours, but the remaining time is available for consultation and groupwork).
 - an expected additional workload of 6 hours per week of self-directed study and/or groupwork.
 Student understanding of subject content (i.e. from lectures, tutorial activities and assigned readings) will be frequently assessed through small weekly quizzes. Tutorials will typically begin with a revision of the previous week’s quiz, and a discussion of any common difficulties or misconceptions that the quiz revealed. As such, these quizzes provide teaching staff with frequent feedback about what has been learned, and identify any topics that need to be revisited.

 The remaining assessment tasks require students to engage with real stakeholders within a real organisation in order to complete them. In the early weeks of the subject, students will be asked to nominate organisations that can act as suitable case-studies. These must be organisations that rely heavily on IT, and with whom the student has a high degree of familiarity and access. Groups will be formed around the most suitable organisations, and these organisations will be the focus of the remaining assessment tasks. Students will need to work collaboratively to develop a shared understanding of the organisation and it’s needs. Each student will then need to work independently to draw on this shared understanding and propose an initiative that the organisation could undertake.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32560 Information Systems Architecture Design | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Model key aspects of the IT landscape of an organization and the forces that shape it, as a pragmatic set of enterprise architecture artefacts. (B.1)
SLO2: Bridge communication gaps between business-oriented and IT-oriented actors, and between strategic-level and tactical-level actors. (E.1)
SLO3: Plan IT initiatives with a sufficient level of detail that key stakeholders can make informed decisions. (C.1)
SLO4: Draw software architecture diagrams that are useful, easy to understand, and reflect the reality of how these systems are built. (D.1)
SLO5: Apply key software architecture principles and patterns for both the process (i.e. how to "do" architecture well) and the result (i.e. what good and bad architecture looks like). (D.1)
